pron.heading: Pronunciation tools
pron.preview: Validate Jyutping entries, inspect tone contours, and surface lexicon matches before you lock in a vocal line.
pron.description: Search by Jyutping or tone code to confirm syllable accuracy, review matched entries, and capture usage notes for lyric writing.
pron.numericIntro: Cantonese lyricists map the six open-syllable tone indices (1–6) to the chant "394052" so the sounded digits saam1, gau2, sei3, ling4, ng5, ji6 mirror the tones they describe.
pron.numericDescription: The extended chant "394052786"—documented in Cantonese phonology guides—anchors lyric drafting because each digit carries the contour singers expect. The table summarises the core mapping used before checked tones enter a melody.
pron.numericCheckedNote: Digits 7-8-6 (chat1, baat3, luk6) share pitch contours with tones 1, 3, and 6 yet surface only on checked syllables ending in -p/-t/-k.
pron.numericSourceEnglishLabel: English overview: "Cantonese phonology" (Wikipedia) — explains the "394052786" mnemonic.
pron.numericSourceChineseLabel: Chinese source: "Cantonese Tones" Wikipedia — includes the nine-tone formula "394052786".

numericTable.caption: Cantonese tone index mapped to lyricist mnemonic digits

pron.jyutpingIntro: Every Cantonese syllable can be analysed as an optional initial consonant, a vowel-based final, and a tone. The LSHK Jyutping scheme records that structure as <initial><final><tone digit>, which keeps lyric stress aligned with the spoken contour.

jyutpingDetails.structure: Write syllables as <initial><final><tone digit>; for example ngo5 = initial "ng" + final "o" + tone 5, while aa3 has no initial and starts directly with the final.
jyutpingDetails.onset: Jyutping recognises 19 initials. When a syllable lacks an initial (a "null initial" in Cantonese phonology) the spelling simply begins with the final, e.g. aa3 or oeng2.
jyutpingDetails.tones: Tone digits 1–6 map to the six Cantonese tone contours; checked syllables ending in -p/-t/-k reuse tone numbers 1, 3, or 6 instead of introducing extra digits.
jyutpingDetails.rhymeLink: Finals (rimes) carry the vowel nucleus and coda. The table below lists the authorised finals used by the LSHK scheme and by the rhyme search input.

pron.jyutpingConsonantsDescription: These initials appear at the beginning of a syllable. Combine one of them (or none, for vowel-initial syllables) with a rime and tone digit to form a full Jyutping spelling.
pron.rhymeDescription: In Cantonese phonology the rime (韻/韻母) contains the vowel nucleus plus any ending consonant. Syllables that share a rime form natural rhyme families—enter any final below to anchor the rhyme search.

rhymeTable.caption: Common Jyutping finals for rhyme search

pron.rhymeListNote: Finals are case-sensitive and should be entered in lowercase to match Jyutping conventions.
pron.rhymeSourceRime: Cantonese syllable structure and rime explanation (Wikipedia)

langHints.zhHk: Labeled as 'zh-HK': typically used in everyday speech, pop culture, and online language. This tag is for reference only—actual usage may overlap or shift, and will be refined over time. Compared to 'written', colloquial words are closer to daily spoken contexts.
langHints.zhTw: Labeled as 'zh-TW': typically found in formal texts, news, books, and official documents, representing the written register of Chinese. This tag is for reference only—actual usage may overlap or shift, and will be refined over time. Compared to 'colloquial', written words tend to be more formal and standardized.
